![What are VVS diamonds?](https://api.dataforseo.com/cdn/i/10031145-2330-0066-0000-d9c9b410a038:4)
VVS diamonds are `high-quality stones with a clarity grade of "Very Very Slightly Included,"` meaning they contain microscopic imperfections that are extremely difficult for a trained gemologist to see under 10x magnification.[[1]](https://www.frostnyc.com/blogs/news/how-much-are-vvs-diamonds)[[2]](https://www.brilliantearth.com/guides/vvs-diamond-clarity/)

### Understanding VVS Grades

- **VVS1:** The higher of the two grades; inclusions are so minute that they are virtually impossible to detect under 10x magnification.[[1]](https://stienhardt.com/blogs/education/vvs-vs-vs-diamonds/)[[2]](https://www.brilliantearth.com/guides/vvs-diamond-clarity/)
- **VVS2:** Contains slightly more noticeable inclusions than VVS1 under magnification, but the stone remains completely clean to the naked eye.[[1]](https://www.brilliantearth.com/guides/vvs-diamond-clarity/)[[2]](https://www.rarecarat.com/blog/diamond-ring-tips/what-are-vvs-diamonds)
- **Rarity:** VVS diamonds sit just below Flawless and Internally Flawless on the grading scale and make up less than 1% of all gem-quality diamonds.[[1]](https://www.brilliantearth.com/guides/vvs-diamond-clarity/)

### Cost and Value

- **Natural vs. Lab-Grown:** Natural VVS diamonds command high prices based on carat, cut, and color, often ranging from thousands to tens of thousands of dollars. Lab-grown VVS diamonds offer the same visual clarity at a fraction of the cost (frequently 75% to 85% less).[[1]](https://www.rarecarat.com/blog/diamond-ring-tips/what-are-vvs-diamonds)[[2]](https://www.frostnyc.com/blogs/news/how-much-are-vvs-diamonds)[[3]](https://www.google.com/search?q=product&prds=pvt:hg,productid:17931089033214863728,catalogid:13538872715493005114,gpcid:17267272621921123145&ibp=oshop)[[4]](https://www.google.com/search?q=product&prds=pvt:hg,productid:13032944657306905155,catalogid:971856948173712583,gpcid:13299966415506932651&ibp=oshop)
- **Are They Worth It?:** Because lower grades like VS1 or VS2 are also "eye-clean" (meaning no flaws can be seen without a magnifying glass), VVS diamonds are usually only necessary or visually advantageous for large stones (over 3 carats) or open step-cuts like emerald or Asscher shapes.[[1]](https://www.youtube.com/shorts/6rCwnuQryew)[[2]](https://www.rarecarat.com/blog/diamond-ring-tips/what-are-vvs-diamonds)[[3]](https://stienhardt.com/blogs/education/vvs-vs-vs-diamonds/)
